title: AP Japanese Language and Culture
summary: Read Japanese notices and viewpoints, explain source limits and construct clear thematic responses.
frameworkNote: Checked against the revised 2026-27 framework on 15 October 2026: six thematic units and a course project supporting exam speaking tasks. The 2027 project packet is due for release in January 2027. These original fictional text scenarios are practice, not authentic cultural sources or a completed project. Add authentic target-language research, listening, conversation and teacher feedback; text answers do not assess pronunciation or oral proficiency.

modules.title: Extract details from a community notice
modules.focus: Families and communities: use particles for time, place and action.
explanation: Particles identify relationships. In “土曜日に公民館で会います”, に marks the scheduled time and で marks the place of the meeting: “We will meet at the community centre on Saturday.” A place where an action occurs usually takes で; existence statements such as “公民館にいます” use に.

A notice may omit the subject when it is clear from context. Read the deadline and participation condition before replying. The original fictional examples practise communication; they do not establish that every Japanese-speaking family takes part in the same activities.

workedExample.prompt: A notice says “金曜日までに申し込んでください。” Ask how to apply.
steps: Interpret までに as a deadline: apply by Friday.
Ask “どうやって申し込めばいいですか。” (How should I apply?)

misconception.claim: に and で are interchangeable whenever a place is named.
misconception.correction: Their roles differ: existence or destination and the location of an action are distinct relationships.

questions.prompt: Choose the particle: “図書館＿勉強します。”
questions.hint: Studying is an action at a location.
questions.answer: “図書館で勉強します。” (I study at the library.)
checkpoints: Chooses で
Connects it to an action

questions.prompt: What does “月曜日までに” mean?
questions.hint: The に makes a deadline expression.
questions.answer: By Monday.
checkpoints: Identifies a deadline
Does not translate it as from Monday

questions.prompt: Interpret 「水を持ってきてもいいですが、食べ物は持ち込まないでください」.
questions.answer: Water may be brought. Food should not be brought in. The water permission is not a requirement.
checkpoints: Water may be brought.
Food should not be brought in.
The water permission is not a requirement.

questions.prompt: Ask politely in Japanese whether beginners can attend.
questions.answer: 「初心者でも参加できますか。」 初心者 identifies beginners. The question asks about eligibility rather than timing.
checkpoints: 「初心者でも参加できますか。」
初心者 identifies beginners.
The question asks about eligibility rather than timing.

notes.title: Extract details from a community notice in depth
paragraphs: Japanese notices distinguish an event time from a deadline. 木曜日までに asks for completion by Thursday, while 木曜日から marks a starting point. The particle に in a deadline expression helps mark the point by which an action is completed; まで can also describe an activity continuing until a time. A polite question with でしょうか should request a genuinely missing detail. Read requirements such as 持ってきてください separately from optional permissions. Knowing an activity's topic is not enough to determine what participants must do before attending.

workedExamples.prompt: Original notice: 「土曜日に料理教室を開きます。木曜日までに申し込んでください。エプロンを持ってきてください。」 Reply.
steps: Saturday is the class; Thursday is the application deadline; an apron is requested.
「料理教室に参加したいです。何時に始まるのでしょうか。エプロンを持っていきます。」
workedExamples.conclusion: The reply addresses participation, materials and the missing start time.

flashcards.front: 木曜日までに means what?
持ってきてください requests what?

modules.title: Read contrast and reported opinion
modules.focus: Language and culture: distinguish a source’s view from a fact.
explanation: “と思います” marks a thought or opinion, while “と言っています” reports what someone says. In “先生はこの表現が丁寧だと言っています”, the teacher is the source of the judgement that the expression is polite. Keep that attribution in a summary.

Register depends on situation and relationship. Polite forms can be appropriate in one exchange without proving social distance in every context. Analyse a particular interaction and avoid broad claims about national personality. Contrast markers such as しかし and でも help reveal how an argument qualifies its first point.

workedExample.prompt: Interpret “この言葉は短くて便利です。でも、正式なメールでは使いません。”
steps: Identify the benefit: the word is short and convenient.
Identify the restriction: the speaker does not use it in formal email. This is a contextual choice, not a claim that the word is always wrong.

misconception.claim: A reported opinion becomes an established fact.
misconception.correction: Attribution tells you whose judgement is being presented, not whether it has been independently verified.

questions.prompt: What does “便利だと思います” express?
questions.answer: The speaker thinks it is convenient.
checkpoints: Identifies opinion
Preserves the judgement

questions.prompt: How would you report that a friend says a word is difficult?
questions.answer: “友達はこの言葉が難しいと言っています。”
checkpoints: Attributes to the friend
Uses the reporting structure

questions.prompt: Interpret 「便利だと言う人もいますが、私は少し分かりにくいと思います」.
questions.hint: Separate some people's view from 私.
hints: Separate some people's view from 私.
questions.answer: Some people call it convenient. The speaker thinks it is a little difficult to understand. The sentence does not measure which view is more common.
checkpoints: Some people call it convenient.
The speaker thinks it is a little difficult to understand.
The sentence does not measure which view is more common.

questions.prompt: Write a bounded Japanese observation about one formal message.
questions.answer: 「このメールでは、書き手は丁寧な表現を使っています。」 The observation concerns this email. It does not establish all people's language choices.
checkpoints: 「このメールでは、書き手は丁寧な表現を使っています。」
The observation concerns this email.
It does not establish all people's language choices.

notes.title: Read contrast and reported opinion in depth
paragraphs: Attribution in Japanese can use によると for a source or と思います for a speaker's judgement. The contrast marker が may connect two propositions without negating either. 必ずしも followed by a negative means not necessarily and should not be read as a universal rejection. Register choices also depend on the relationship, medium and purpose of an exchange. A polite form in one message supports an observation about that interaction. It cannot by itself establish a person's complete identity or how everyone in a community communicates.

workedExamples.prompt: Original text: 「この言葉はよく使われますが、田中さんは報告書では使わないと言っています。」
steps: The first clause says the word is often used.
田中さん ... と言っています attributes the report-specific choice to Tanaka.
workedExamples.conclusion: The statement contrasts common use with one person's contextual decision.

flashcards.front: 必ずしも ... ない means what?
Does polite language establish everyone's behaviour?

modules.title: Connect music, action and meaning
modules.focus: Art and creativity: prepare an evidence-based research note.
explanation: A recording, instrument or written score can provide evidence about a musical product. Rehearsing or performing is a practice. A participant’s explanation of why they take part can support an interpretation of perspective. Keep those forms of evidence distinct and connected.

For authentic research, record a source’s creator, date, place and relevant passage or timestamp. Use actual Japanese-language sources and follow the official exam-year packet when available. The fictional statements here are language exercises and cannot serve as project evidence or assess listening and speaking proficiency.

workedExample.prompt: Read “地域の人と交流するために、毎月コンサートを開いています。”
steps: Identify the activity: holding a concert every month.
Explain the stated purpose: interacting with local people. ために marks purpose here.

misconception.claim: A concert’s musical style alone proves its social purpose.
misconception.correction: A purpose claim needs contextual evidence, such as participant testimony or documentation.

questions.prompt: What frequency is expressed by 毎月?
questions.answer: Every month.
checkpoints: Identifies monthly frequency
Does not say every week

questions.prompt: Paraphrase the stated aim in English.
questions.hint: Focus on 交流するために.
questions.answer: The organisers hold concerts to interact with people in the local community.
checkpoints: Keeps the stated aim
Does not invent a national custom

questions.prompt: Paraphrase 「楽器は変えましたが、歌詞は変えていません」.
questions.hint: Keep changed and unchanged features distinct.
hints: Keep changed and unchanged features distinct.
Do not invent a new tune.
questions.answer: The instruments were changed. The lyrics have not been changed. The statement does not specify whether the melody changed.
checkpoints: The instruments were changed.
The lyrics have not been changed.
The statement does not specify whether the melody changed.

questions.prompt: Explain in Japanese why a poster cannot alone establish audience feelings.
questions.answer: 「ポスターには日時や出演者が書かれています。」 「それだけでは観客の感想は分かりません。」 「観客の考えを調べるには、関連する聞き取りなどが必要です。」
checkpoints: 「ポスターには日時や出演者が書かれています。」
「それだけでは観客の感想は分かりません。」
「観客の考えを調べるには、関連する聞き取りなどが必要です。」

notes.title: Connect music, action and meaning in depth
paragraphs: A musical source may describe an activity and explain its purpose without showing that the purpose was achieved. ために can express an aim, while ように can describe an intended state or ability in suitable constructions. Keep frequency precise: 月に二回 means twice a month, whereas 二か月に一回 means once every two months. A recording can support observations about sound, while an interview supplies an attributed account of meaning. Document their creator and context before linking them. An invented exercise cannot be treated as evidence of an actual community's practice.

workedExamples.prompt: Original invented interview: 「新しいメンバーが歌えるように、ゆっくり練習しています。」
steps: The group practises slowly.
The purpose is to enable new members to sing; paraphrase: 「新しい人が参加しやすいように、練習の速さを変えています。」
workedExamples.conclusion: This explains a rehearsal choice, not every performance's tempo.

flashcards.front: 二か月に一回 means what?
What does a participant interview directly support?
flashcards.back: An attributed account of that participant's experience or explanation.

modules.title: Report a survey and its limits
modules.focus: Science and technology: separate measured data from possibility.
explanation: A percentage describes a defined group. “回答者の半分” means half of the respondents, not half of all residents. When reading a chart, check the number surveyed and whether people could choose more than one response.

“かもしれません” expresses possibility: “時間を節約できるかもしれません” means it may be possible to save time. This is weaker than claiming that a tool already saved time. A technology argument should name who benefits, who may lack access and what evidence would test the predicted effect.

workedExample.prompt: A fictional survey finds that 18 of 60 students use a timetable app.
steps: Calculate 18 ÷ 60 = 30%.
Report “回答した学生の30パーセントがこのアプリを使っています”, retaining the surveyed group.

misconception.claim: A survey of one class directly represents all students.
misconception.correction: A broader claim needs a justified sample and careful attention to the population.

questions.prompt: What does 半分 mean in a chart caption?
questions.answer: Half, or 50 percent.
checkpoints: Gives one half
Connects to 50%

questions.prompt: Add uncertainty to “便利です”.
questions.answer: “便利かもしれません。” (It may be convenient.)
checkpoints: Uses the correct connection
Expresses possibility

questions.prompt: Report 4 of 20 respondents lacking internet access in Japanese.
questions.answer: 「回答者の20パーセントはインターネットを利用できません。」 4/20 equals 20%. The statement refers to respondents, not all residents.
checkpoints: 「回答者の20パーセントはインターネットを利用できません。」
4/20 equals 20%.
The statement refers to respondents, not all residents.

questions.prompt: Explain why 100 downloads do not establish 100 satisfied users.
questions.answer: 「一人が何度もダウンロードすることがあります。」 「ダウンロード数だけでは満足度は分かりません。」 「実際の利用者の経験を調べる必要があります。」
checkpoints: 「一人が何度もダウンロードすることがあります。」
「ダウンロード数だけでは満足度は分かりません。」
「実際の利用者の経験を調べる必要があります。」

notes.title: Report a survey and its limits in depth
paragraphs: Counts of activity and counts of people answer different questions. 利用回数 means number of uses, while 利用者数 means number of users. Repeated visits by one person can raise the former without raising the latter. Percentages need a stated reference group, and 回答者のうち keeps the respondents visible. A change from twenty to thirty percent is ten percentage points, not ten percent relative growth. Use かもしれません for an untested possibility and identify the observation required to support a stronger claim about access, learning or efficiency.

workedExamples.prompt: Invented survey: 12 of 30 respondents use a tool; later 12 of 24 do.
steps: Compute 40% and 50%; the number twelve does not change.
「利用者の割合は10ポイント増えましたが、人数は12人のままです。」
workedExamples.conclusion: The changed denominator explains the higher share.

flashcards.front: 回答者のうち means what?
かもしれません expresses what?

modules.title: Describe a change in everyday routine
modules.focus: Contemporary life: connect past experience and present habits.
explanation: “以前は” sets an earlier situation and “今は” contrasts the present. “以前は歩いて通学していましたが、今はバスで通っています” means the speaker used to walk to school but now travels by bus. The contrast is about this speaker, not every student.

Use temporal connectors to organise an account. “引っ越してから” means after moving, while “引っ越す前に” means before moving. The form before these expressions affects the sequence. A clear explanation includes the change and its practical consequence rather than a list of unrelated events.

workedExample.prompt: Describe studying at a different library after moving.
steps: State “引っ越してから、駅の近くの図書館を使っています。”
Explain the meaning: since moving, the speaker has been using the library near the station.

misconception.correction: It can also mark a starting point or sequence, depending on the construction.

questions.prompt: Translate “授業が終わってから”.
questions.hint: The て-form links the completed event to what follows.
questions.answer: After class finishes.
checkpoints: Identifies the sequence
Does not say before class

questions.prompt: How would you say “before going to school”?
questions.hint: Use dictionary form before 前に.
questions.answer: “学校に行く前に.”
checkpoints: Uses 行く
Places 前に after the verb

questions.prompt: Choose the correct forms: 「出かける／出かけた 前に、窓を閉めます」 and 「食べる／食べた 後で、勉強します」.
questions.hint: Notice 前に and 後で.
hints: Notice 前に and 後で.
Match the verb form to the sequence.
questions.answer: 出かける前に is correct. 食べた後で is correct. The first action is before going out; studying follows eating.
checkpoints: 出かける前に is correct.
食べた後で is correct.
The first action is before going out; studying follows eating.

questions.prompt: Write a Japanese account of a move and a changed library routine.
questions.answer: 「引っ越してから、駅の近くの図書館を使っています。」 The move comes before the changed routine. The sentence identifies the library near the station.
checkpoints: 「引っ越してから、駅の近くの図書館を使っています。」
The move comes before the changed routine.
The sentence identifies the library near the station.

notes.title: Describe a change in everyday routine in depth
paragraphs: Japanese temporal constructions organise the relationship between actions. Before 前に, a verb commonly takes its dictionary form: 出かける前に. Before 後で, the completed form appears: 食べた後で. てから also places one action before another. When describing a change in routine, 以前は and 今は establish a contrast, while a concrete event explains why the routine changed. Keep the statement's scope personal when the source is a personal account. A change in one narrator's journey does not demonstrate a general national transport trend. A sequence marker alone does not prove a causal relationship.

workedExamples.prompt: Describe a fictional change after a nearby pool opens.
steps: 「以前は遠いプールまでバスで行っていました。」 establishes the previous routine.
「近くにプールができてから、歩いて通っています。」 gives the change and current journey.
workedExamples.conclusion: The sequence connects the new location to the shorter journey.

flashcards.front: 出かける前に means what?

flashcards.back: Places the following action after the first.

modules.title: Propose a small response to a wider issue
modules.focus: Global contexts: explain purpose and evaluate outcomes.
explanation: A proposal should name an action, a purpose and a realistic constraint. “ごみを減らすために” means “in order to reduce rubbish”. The phrase identifies an intention; it does not prove that the action achieved the reduction.

For a fictional reusable-cup trial, distinguish cups distributed from disposable cups avoided. Cleaning, participation and replacement rates affect the outcome. Compare similar periods and consider other changes. This keeps a persuasive argument connected to evidence rather than presenting an imagined success as a result.

workedExample.prompt: Propose a fictional school cup-return scheme.
steps: Write “ごみを減らすために、繰り返し使えるコップを導入したいです。”
Explain that you would like to introduce reusable cups to reduce rubbish, then specify that cleaning arrangements must be checked.

misconception.claim: Stating a purpose demonstrates the result.
misconception.correction: A purpose is an intention; measured outcomes require separate evidence.

questions.prompt: What does ために express in the proposal?
questions.hint: Look at the goal before it.
questions.answer: Purpose: in order to reduce rubbish.
checkpoints: Identifies purpose
Does not claim a completed result

questions.prompt: What should be measured to evaluate the scheme?
questions.hint: Compare the relevant outcome over similar periods.
questions.answer: Counts of disposable cups used, with records of reusable-cup returns and cleaning, before and during the trial.
checkpoints: Measures actual use
Checks implementation

questions.prompt: Write a Japanese proposal to add clearer signs to recycling bins.
questions.answer: 「ごみを正しく分けるために、分かりやすい表示を付けたいです。」 The action is adding clear labels. Sorting accuracy still needs observation.
checkpoints: 「ごみを正しく分けるために、分かりやすい表示を付けたいです。」
The action is adding clear labels.
Sorting accuracy still needs observation.

questions.prompt: State one condition and one outcome measure for a reusable-cup trial in Japanese.
hints: Do not count distribution as avoided waste.
questions.answer: 「洗う方法と返す場所を決める必要があります。」 「配ったコップの数だけでは効果は分かりません。」 「使い捨てコップの使用量を比較します。」
checkpoints: 「洗う方法と返す場所を決める必要があります。」
「配ったコップの数だけでは効果は分かりません。」
「使い捨てコップの使用量を比較します。」

notes.title: Propose a small response to a wider issue in depth
paragraphs: A proposal should state an action, a reason and the conditions needed for it to work. ために can identify a purpose without proving a result. A conditional such as なら can frame a recommendation around a stated situation, while 必要があります identifies a requirement. For a repair scheme, distinguish attendance from repairs that remain useful after the event. Tools, supervision and safe access affect implementation. A measured reduction in replacement purchases requires more evidence than a count of repaired items, because some items might not otherwise have been replaced.

workedExamples.prompt: Propose a fictional school bag-repair activity.
steps: 「かばんを長く使うために、修理の会を開きたいです。」
「適切な道具と、作業を指導する人が必要です。」
workedExamples.conclusion: Check continued use after repairs before claiming fewer purchases.

flashcards.front: 必要があります means what?
flashcards.back: There is a need or requirement.
The outcome linked to the proposal, such as continued use.
